articleTitle: Characterisation of resonance modes of a magnetron cavity using MAGIC-an FD-TD code
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Effective Microwave CAD Tools (Ref. No. 1999/064)
abstract: It is demonstrated here that MAGIC code provides an efficient way to obtain the important information for magnetron design, i.e. the resonance spectrum and mode patterns of the cavity. It is expected that this FD-TD code can be equally effective in characterising resonance features of other microwave devices and components.

articleTitle: Filter design using automatic parameterization of 3D arbitrary geometries
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Effective Microwave CAD Tools (Ref. No. 1999/064)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate a new approach for the synthesis, design and optimization of electronic filters in a high volume production environment for modern digital communication systems by using automatic parameterization of 3D geometries. The design of waveguide bandpass filters by EPFIL is considered. EPFIL is described itself, and the two actual filter implementations are presented. Measurement on a fabricated bandpass filter confirms the accuracy of design procedure.

articleTitle: An introduction to Electronics Workbench for designing circuits and PCBs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Effective Microwave CAD Tools (Ref. No. 1999/064)
abstract: Electronics Workbench is a mixed-mode SPICE-based electronics design and simulation tool. This paper describes the main features of the software, the advantages for the circuit designer, and the link to Electronics Workbench Layout for producing PCB layouts.

articleTitle: SCALC: low-cost microwave network analysis and optimisation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Effective Microwave CAD Tools (Ref. No. 1999/064)
abstract: SCALC is low-cost analysis and optimisation package for linear (small-signal) RF networks. It makes extensive use of S-parameters, and thus SCALC is particularly suitable for applications in the VHF to microwave region. SCALC can analyse networks of up to 20 circuit elements, comprising passive components (with parasitic reactances and finite Q) and active components that are characterised by files of frequency-dependent S-parameter data. The results of an SCALC analysis are also S-parameters, which can be saved to similar datafiles, and can later be recalled into a higher-level system analysis. Unlike most low-cost analysis packages, SCALC includes a powerful optimiser. This paper will introduce the main features of SCALC and present some simple examples of its use.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Effective Microwave CAD Tools (Ref. No. 1999/064)
abstract: This paper has outlined the rationale for using the Real Frequency Technique as a method of synthesising matching networks and reviewed one very low-cost program that implements this technique, namely the RFT Impedance Matching Toolbox program. It has been shown that this program is constrained to synthesise only lowpass networks and this inhibits its application to bandpass matching problems.

articleTitle: Nonlinear microwave circuit analysis using the genetic algorithms toolbox in MATLAB
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Effective Microwave CAD Tools (Ref. No. 1999/064)
abstract: This paper will show how it is possible to use a relatively inexpensive MATLAB toolbox together with MATLAB to apply a genetic algorithm to a both the sample balance and harmonic balance techniques, and then subsequently solve a variety of nonlinear microwave circuits. The extension of this method to multitone circuit analysis (in which the tones are noncommensurate) will also be highlighted. One of the strengths of genetic algorithms is their relative transparency to the problem being solved. Auxiliary information (such as a Jacobian) is not required and there is great flexibility in the choice of the fitness evaluation function. This allows the development of a frequency-domain sample balance technique, in which the error is formed in the time-domain but the voltages are updated in the frequency-domain. It will be shown that this novel application of genetic algorithms yields a nonlinear microwave circuit solver that is robust, can ultimately handle any number of noncommensurate input tones, and does not assume any a priori knowledge of circuit behaviour in the steady state.

articleTitle: Experience of developing and using CAD tools for III-V FETs effectively in a nonideal world
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Effective Microwave CAD Tools (Ref. No. 1999/064)
abstract: This paper describes the experience gained in developing and using CAD tools for the design of low distortion and nonlinear FET circuits using III-V technology. It includes a description of the CAD packages used, key features required in the CAD packages for realistic simulation, techniques for small and large signal "quick look" assessment for choosing bias and load and some example circuits where the tools have been used successfully.
